Thanks for asking.

Commie or Socialist is often used as a pejorative in the USA, but there is much about these systems that works well.

The case of the marina you have provided might be one of the many instances where the free market fails to provide a socially optimum solution. This example is similar to the tragedy of the commons, I think.

Lets say there are 10 people who use the marina, and you are one of these lucky few. If the marina isn't dredged, nobody will be able to use it. So, what the 10 yachtsmen are all hoping is that somebody else dredges the marina. (It is a horrible job, time consuming, energy draining and costly.)

You decide to keep your nerve and just get by, despite how bad it gets, hoping, like everybody else, that somebody else will find it so intolerable that they decide to dredge it themself. They might do so, hoping that it would provide a good example to everybody else, and that somebody else would do it next time, as it would be "their turn". But everybody else buys champagne with the money they saved by not dredging the marina, and continue to enjoy easy access. I

In a situation like this, somebody might try and dredge "their half" of the marina. Unfortunately, the tide and sands don't work that way. They shift and you need to dredge the whole lot.

What happens later? Well, the good example chap simply refuses to do it again. Another chap decides to use a different marina when it gets too bad, rather than fixing that one, and everybody else is left with an unusable marina and can't sail.

Lets say the sailors voluntarily club together, to pay for the dredging. You think it is a good idea too, so chip in the required amount. One guy though, there is always somebody, thinks to himself, I will let the others pay for the dredging, not pay myself and buy some champagne to drink instead. This annoys everybody. They hate that guy, but can't do anything about it.

In these situations, an economically stable outcome has arrived, but it is not socially optimum. (Nash won a Nobel prize on this.)

For an optimum social solution, a higher entity needs to be created, which can charge the yachtsmen for the overheads of using the marina. (It could charge visiting yachts, too.) So, the yachting club is formed.

Similar issues to this include the provision of lighthouses and the surfacing of private roads shared by a number of residents along the way.
